name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 20, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:03 p.m., on June
20, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 17, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with the City's Real Property Negotiators Pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54956.8. Real property Denoted as Assessor's Parcel No. 784-291-01
  with a Common Street Address of 24701 San Doval, Mission Viejo, California,

City Council Minutes  1  June 20, 2011
   Commonly Known as O'Neill Elementary School Owned by Saddleback Valley
  Unified School District The Negotiating Parties are: City of Mission Viejo; Dennis
  Wilberg, City Manager, Irwin Bornstein, Assistant City Manager, Charles Wilson,
  Director of Community Development, and William Curley, III, City Attorney.
  Owner Negotiators are: Saddleback Valley Unified School District, Clint Harwick,
  Superintendent. Under Negotiation will be the Price and Terms of a Lease-Hold
  Interest in the Real Property.

CS2. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

CS3. Conference with Real Property Negotiator pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8. Property is an approximate 10.5 acre Site commonly referred to as the
  “Former K Mart” located at 28601 Los Alisos Boulevard and Comprised of
  Assessor Parcel Nos. (APNs) 839-161-08 and 839-161-09 owned by Union Dominion
  Realty/Pacific Los Alisos L.P. (“UDR”). CDA negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, City
  Manager/CDA Executive Director, Charles Wilson, Director of Community
  Development, James Williams, Economic Advisor, Celeste Brady, CDA Counsel,
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney. Owner’s negotiators: Jeremy Cyr of UDR
  and John Ramirez, Kerra Carlson of Rutan & Tucker, Frank Spevacek of Rosenow
  Spevacek Group, ad Peter Whittingham of Curt Pringle Associates, all on behalf of
  UDR. Under negotiation: potential acquisition and/or disposition of real property
  interests for long term affordable housing and the price and terms of payment
  therefore related to the above-listed property. Factors affecting price and terms
  under negotiation: recorded covenants, scope of development of property,
  affordable housing requirements. Factors affecting time of payment: conditions to
  closing, due diligence period, and schedule of development and development of
  affordable housing.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council provided direction to staff in Closed
Session but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Musical Performance by Violinist Rachelle Schouten

City Council Minutes  2  June 20, 2011
   The City Council Members heard a musical presentation from violinist Rachelle
  Schouten.

P2.  Recognize City Volunteers, for their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Leckness presented certificates of appreciation to Mary Lou Moncino and Pauline
  Kawczynski for their volunteer hours with the Senior Community Activity Team
  (SCAT.) Animal Services Center volunteers, Harriet LeGrand and Linda Mosely, were
  unable to attend the meeting.

P3.  Recognize the Viejo Little League’s AAA Minor Team (Oregon Ducks) for Placing
  First in the District 68 Little League Tournament of Champions

  Mayor Leckness presented certificates of commendation to the coaches and members of
  the Mission Viejo "Oregon Ducks" Little League team.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Joyce Saltzgiver, liaison to the City from Casta del Sol: read a letter from resident Russ Atkinson
regarding his disappointment with traffic signal synchronization in the City.

David Lowenthal, M.V.: complained that a food vendor at the DAWG walk served animal meat
products and that the City Council supports a Bunny Days event each year, yet they approved the
shooting of rabbits at Casta del Sol.

Dan Avery, M.V.: announced that he watched the City Council budget workshop on television
last week and he feels that one Council Member's comments were deceptive and unrealistic.

Joe Alanes, M.V.: requested the City Council's support for the Modjeska Playhouse Potocki
Center lease proposal.

Joshua Stecker, Rancho Santa Margarita: expressed support for a Modjeska Playhouse lease of
the Potocki Center.

Christopher Sullivan, Rancho Santa Margarita: stated that Modjeska Playhouse would serve a
need that does not currently exist in Mission Viejo.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed concern with police and fire overtime costs and asked if
anyone from the City of Mission Viejo is investigating his concerns.

City Council Minutes  3  June 20, 2011
 Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: announced that she brought a borrowed dog to the DAWG walk and
she had a great time. She also discussed her attendance at the Community of Character gala and
stated that the City's character program is extremely important for our youth.

Bob Hayes, M.V.: discussed national holidays and expressed his support for the recognition of
Independence Day. Mr. Hayes encouraged residents to attend the character film screening of
John Adams in the Council Chamber on June 26.

Patricia Sullivan, M.V: presented a written comment in support of the Modjeska Playhouse lease
proposal for the Potocki Center.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 9, 11, 16, 19, 21, 22, and 24 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Check Register dated May 27, 2011, in the amount of $490,658.43

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated June 3, 2011 in the amount of $705,858.33

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2011

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  4  June 20, 2011
 6.  Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2011

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2011

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Facilities District No 92-1 - Annual Special Tax for Fiscal
  Year 2011-12

  Adopted Resolution 11-38 Establishing an Annual Special tax for Fiscal Year 2011-12
  for Community Facilities District No. 92-1 (Mission Viejo Freeway Center).

10.  Professional Services Agreement for Printing and Related Services for the City
  Outlook and Leisure Time

  (1) Approved the Professional Services Agreement with PSB Integrated Marketing for
  design and related services for four issues of Outlook and eight issues of Leisure Time
  for the period of July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2013, in the amount of $204,788.00; and
  (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to PSB Integrated Marketing for the period of
  July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2012, in an amount not to exceed $102,394.00 pending
  adoption of the 2011-2013 budget by City Council.

12.  Annual Routine Park, Right-of-Way, and Facility Electrical, Lighting Maintenance
  Repair and Replacement

  (1) Approved Third Amendment to the existing contract with C & D Electric for the
  period July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2013, to increase the contract amount by an amount
  not to exceed $531,460.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to C & D
  Electric for the period July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2012, in an amount not to exceed
  $265,730.00 pending adoption of the Fiscal Year 2011-2013 budget by the City Council.

13.  Annual Routine Janitorial and Related Services at Various Park Sites and Facilities

  (1) Approved the Third Amendment for the Annual Routine Janitorial and Related
  Services at Various Park Sites and Facilities contract to Vocational Visions for the period
  of July 1, 2011, to June 30, 2013, in an amount not to exceed $242,776.00; and (2)
  authorized staff to issue a purchase order to Vocational Visions for the period of July 1,
  2011, through June 30, 2012, in an amount not to exceed $121,388.00, pending adoption
  of the 2011-13 Budget by the City Council.

City Council Minutes  5  June 20, 2011
 14.  Janitorial and Related Services at the Mission Viejo Animal Shelter, Thomas R.
  Potocki Conference Center and Corporate Yard Administration Building

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract for the subject services to Great
  Cleaning Services Inc. (DBA GCS, Inc.) for the period July 1, 2011, through June 30,
  2013, in an amount not to exceed $40,100.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase
  order to Great Cleaning Services Inc. for the period July 1, 2011, to June 30, 2012, in an
  amount not to exceed $20,500.00, pending adoption of the 2011-2013 budget by the City
  Council.

15.  Purchase of Pool Chemicals for City Aquatic and Recreation Centers

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract for the subject services to Alpha
  Water Systems Inc. for the period July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2013, in an amount not
  to exceed $203,600.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Alpha Water
  Systems for the period July 1, 2011, to June 30, 2012, in an amount not to exceed
  $101,800.00 pending adoption of the 2011-2013 Budget by the City Council.

17.  Master Plan of Arterial Highways: Renewed Measure M Annual Consistency
  Determination

  Adopted Resolution No. 11-40 Concerning the Status of the Mission Viejo General Plan
  Circulation Element and Confirming that the Circulation Element Does Not Preclude
  Implementation of the Orange County Master Plan of Arterial Highways; and (2) directed
  staff to transmit said resolution to the Orange County Transportation Authority by June
  30, 2011, to maintain the City’s eligibility in receiving Fiscal Year 2011-2012 Renewed
  Measure M (M2) local turnback funds and in pursuing competitive grant funding
  opportunities.

18.  Storm Drain and Water Quality Improvements for Oso Parkway (CIP 207)-
  Rejection of Bids

  (1) Rejected all bids for the project; and (2) authorized staff to re-advertise for
  construction bids for the subject project.

20.  Purchase of Janitorial-Related Paper, Plastic, and Chemical Supplies for City
  Building Facilities

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract to Clean Source in the amount of
  $36,875.00; and (2) approved First Amendment to the existing contract to Waxie Sanitary
  Supply in the amount of $34,711.00 for fiscal year 2011-2012.

City Council Minutes  6  June 20, 2011
 23.  Annual Routine Tree Trimming Contract

  (1) Approved Eighth Amendment to the existing contract with West Coast Arborists, Inc.
  for the period July 1, 2011 through June 30, 2013 to increase the contract amount by an
  amount not to exceed $1,182,158.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to
  West Coast Arborists, Inc for the period July 1, 2011 through June 30, 2012 in an amount
  not to exceed $591,079.00, pending adoption of the 2011-13 Budget by the City Council.

25.  Authorization for Continuing Appropriations and Preliminary FY 2010/11
  Carryovers

  (1) Adopted Resolution 11-41 to Authorize Appropriations Commencing July 1, 2011,
  Based on Prior Year Spending Levels, Until Such Time as the 2011-13 Budget is
  Adopted; and (2) adopted Resolution 11-42 Authorizing, on an Interim Basis, the
  Carryover of FY 2010/11 Year End Encumbrances and Periodic Adjustments to the FY
  2011/12 Budget to Reflect Encumbered FY 2010/11 Balances Until FY 2010/11 is
  Closed Out.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

26.  Review of 2011-13 Proposed Budget

  The City Council Members asked questions of staff regarding the proposed 2011-13
  budget.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed concern that the outline of capital improvement projects
  does not include carryover CIPs such as the proposed dog park.

  No action taken.

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Referring to item number 10 on page 10 of the Minutes, Council Member Schlicht asked
  the City Manager to investigate whether any claims have been filed against the contractor
  which would have triggered a $42,000 increase in the cost of the contract.

City Council Minutes  7  June 20, 2011
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to approve
  the Minutes from the Regular City Council Meeting of June 6, 2011, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

9.  Fourth Quarter Budget Appropriation Adjustments

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she removed this item from the Consent
  Calendar to highlight that the mid-year report omitted the reduction of almost $900,000
  in projected revenue.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to adopt
  Resolution 11-39 Amending the FY 2010/11 Budget for Adjustments to Various
  Revenue and Expenditure Accounts.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

11.  Ordinance Amending Section 9.29.220 to Title 9 of the Municipal Code Pertaining
  to Subdivision Sales and Model Home Directional Signs

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she removed this item from the Consent
  Calendar so she could vote no in consistency with her prior vote on the ordinance.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to adopt
  Ordinance 11-290 Adopting Revisions to Short Term Signage and Use Standards.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht,
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  8  June 20, 2011
 16.  Annual Routine Landscape Maintenance - Marguerite Slope Rehabilitation -
  Contract Area 1

  Council Member Reardon announced that she meant to remove item 10 from the Consent
  Calendar to compliment the City Clerk on a thorough and well-written agenda report.

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report for item 16.

  Council Member Reardon asked questions about the proposed slope renovations, tree
  removal, and the potential re-use of plants.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  approve the Third Amendment to the existing contract with Nieves Landscape, Inc. (A07-
  58C) extending the contract three months and to increase the contract in an amount not to
  exceed $310,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

19.  Annual Routine Street Sweeping Services

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Debbie Kaye, Operations Manager, Sunset Property Services: discussed the services that
  her firm has provided over the past seventeen years and she asked the City Council to
  award a new contract to Sunset based on their recent bid.

  The following spoke in favor of awarding a new contract to Sunset Property Services:
  Ron James, M.V. and Nina Altountash, M.V.

  Michael Alarcon, Rancho Santa Margarita: expressed support for staff’s recommendation
  to extend the contract for 60 days to allow time to carefully analyze and review the
  proposals.

  Brett Barbre, Attorney representing Athens Services: asked when copies of the bid
  packages will be available and stated that Athens is committed to offering a seamless
  transition if the Council awards them a street sweeping contract.

City Council Minutes  9  June 20, 2011
   Gary Clifford, Athens Services: asked why Athens is subject to the evaluation of another
  bidder regarding their competency. He outlined their services in other communities and
  committed to providing the same high-level service in Mission Viejo.

  Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: stated that Sunset does a good job with the street sweeping but
  she also supports staff’s diligence in extending the contract to allow time to evaluate both
  proposals.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  approve Fourth Amendment to the existing contract with Sunset Property Services
  extending the contract two months and to increase the contract in an amount not to
  exceed $65,000.00 to provide staff time to further evaluate the bid proposals.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  By consensus, the Council Members directed staff to return with a recommendation on
  the new street sweeping contract sooner than August 15 if all the information is available.

21.  Annual Routine Tree Trimming Contract - Marguerite Parkway Slope
  Rehabilitation - West Coast Arborists, Inc.

  Council Member Reardon announced that her questions were answered during the
  discussion for item 16.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to approve
  the Seventh Amendment to the existing contract with West Coast Arborists, Inc. to
  increase the contract in an amount not to exceed $40,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

22.  Mission Viejo Library Re-carpeting Project (CIP 319) and City Hall - Notice of
  Completion

  Council Member Reardon commended the Director of Public Services for completing

City Council Minutes  10  June 20, 2011
   this project under budget and she inquired about the leftover funds and a proposed project
  to reupholster furniture at the library.

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay indicated that the remaining monies would be
  returned to the general fund and the upholstery project for the library furniture would
  come from the current operating budget.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  authorize the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange
  and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days
  respectively after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no
  claims or liens being filed with or by the City; and (2) authorize the payment of the final
  retention of $10,826.52, 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of
  Completion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

24.  Mission Viejo Community Development Agency Budget

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed concern with the agenda report and the future of
  redevelopment agency funds.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to (1)
  receive the Proposed FY 2011-13 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Agency; and (2) adopt CDA Resolution 11-09 Amending the FY 2010-11
  Mission Viejo Community Development Agency budget for a Transfer to the Mission
  Viejo Housing Authority.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:40 p.m., Mayor Leckness declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
8:48 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  11  June 20, 2011
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

27.  Community Services Commission Senior Appointment

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to appoint
  Robert Breton to fill the senior member vacancy on the Community Services
  Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

28.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the OCFA
  Board of Directors.

  Steven Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the best place to look for savings is in fire and
  police department overtime and pension costs. He outlined his recent request for
  information from OCFA and stated that he hasn’t received the documents yet.

29.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury stated that there has not been a recent meeting of the
  Foothill/Eastern TCA.

30.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness stated that had nothing to report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

In response to an earlier comment by a member of the public, City Manager Wilberg announced
that the City has been awarded a grant from OCTA to coordinate the signals along Marguerite
Parkway. He noted that the Public Works Director will follow up with the Council and provide
more detail on that particular project as well as a resident’s question related to signals on
Jeronimo Road.

City Council Minutes  12  June 20, 2011
 31.  Mission Viejo Environmental Home Owner Association Request For City To Take
  Over Slope Maintenance for a Portion of a Parcel Along Alicia Parkway

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  The following asked the City Council to support the Mission Viejo Environmental Home
  Owners Association request: Anthony Acetta, President of the Mission Viejo
  Environmental HOA, M.V.; Joe Tully, M.V.; Joe Holtzman, M.V.; and Donna Bourassa,
  M.V.

  City Manager Wilberg noted that staff could have approved this off-agenda however, in
  the past they have been accused of either doing a stealth project or doing something that
  should have been authorized by the City Council.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  assume responsibility for slope maintenance for a portion of a parcel along Alicia
  Parkway and to collaborate with the Mission Viejo Environmental Homeowners
  Association in this endeavor.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Attorney's Report

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that he had nothing to report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

32.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley reminded residents to look at the City’s calendar and events postcard for
upcoming summer activities. The Prelude in the Park will be held Saturday, July 30, 2011, and

City Council Minutes  13  June 20, 2011
 the event - also known as Target’s Symphony in the Cities – has been a huge success every year.
She also congratulated the Viejo Little League “Oregon Ducks” for winning the District 68
Tournament of Champions. She recalled that she spent many hours watching Viejo Little
League games when her own boys played baseball and she was happy that the City Council
could recognize the team earlier in the evening. She also discussed her attendance at the
Capistrano Valley High School Performing Arts Center ground breaking ceremony. The project
is moving forward and the theater is scheduled to be completed in 2012. Council Member
Kelley reminded residents that the City screens movies of character and this month’s movie
supports the word citizenship. John Adams Part I will be shown on Sunday, June 26 in the City
Council Chamber and she encouraged residents to come early to get a good seat. Lastly, Council
Member Kelley announced that this is Deputy Darren Sandberg’s last City Council Meeting.
She stated that Deputy Sandberg has done an outstanding job during his time in Mission Viejo
and she wished him luck in his new job as an instructor at the Sheriff’s Department Academy.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon agreed that Deputy Sandberg will be missed. She also congratulated
the Viejo Little League championship team and she thanked the City volunteers, not just the ones
who were honored earlier in the evening. She noted that the Capistrano Valley High School
graduation ceremony will be held this week and she plans to attend. Additionally, the Marine car
wash and a wheelchair tennis fundraiser will be held on Saturday, June 25. Council Member
Reardon discussed her attendance at the League of California Cities meeting in Sacramento this
past week. It was an excellent conference and she learned a lot, especially about the de-
incorporation efforts for the City of Vernon and she gathered new information during the
Administration Committee that she serves on. Council Member Reardon announced that she
would like to see the Council develop a policy that would allow them to interact more with the
public because she feels that the Council owes that to the residents. Lastly, she provided an
update on the two cancer-stricken children that she has been talking about the past few months.
She shared that both are improving and it is miraculous to see what is happening. Council
Member Reardon asked her colleagues to keep the children in their thoughts and prayers.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht reminded residents of the Fourth of July Street Faire and fireworks
show. She concluded her comments with a quote from Thomas Jefferson, “Above all things I
hope the education of the common people will be attended to, convinced that on their good sense
we may rely with the most security for the preservation of a due degree of liberty.”

City Council Minutes  14  June 20, 2011
 Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Ury stated that he had nothing to report.

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness announced that he will miss Deputy Darren Sandberg, especially the way he
gives scout and student tours at city hall. He noted that Darren’s participation is always the
highlight of the kids’ tour and he expects to hear a lot of good things about Deputy Sandberg in
his new position at the Academy. Mayor Leckness outlined his recent activities including his
attendance at the Bathgate Elementary School car show and the ground breaking of the
Capistrano Valley High School Performing Arts Theater. Mayor Leckness concluded his
comments by thanking Irwin Bornstein. He stated that Irwin has been very important to the City
of Mission Viejo and he wished to acknowledge Irwin before he retires.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:49 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting in memory of Genaro Hernández, to Tuesday, July 5,
2011, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________

Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 5, 2011

City Council Minutes  15  June 20, 2011
